flashcard_questions.q: What is conjunct motion in a melody?
flashcard_questions.a: Movement by step, to the next note up or down in the scale.

flashcard_questions.q: What is disjunct motion in a melody?
flashcard_questions.a: Movement by leap over one or more scale degrees.

flashcard_questions.q: Which term describes a melody that rises and then falls?
How many pitches does the chorus melody of Africa use?
flashcard_questions.a: Only two, giving a very narrow pitch range.

flashcard_questions.q: Which scale does the melody of Africa use in bars 66 to 69?

flashcard_questions.a: A rapid alternation between two adjacent notes.
Small extra notes played quickly before the main note, purely decorative.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the term syllabic mean?
flashcard_questions.a: One note per syllable of text.
One syllable sung across several notes.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a sequence in a melody?
flashcard_questions.a: A melodic phrase repeated at a higher or lower pitch.

flashcard_questions.q: Which articulation marking means smooth and connected?
Which articulation marking means short and detached?
Which curved line joins two notes of the same pitch and combines their durations?
What does pizzicato tell a string player to do?
flashcard_questions.a: Pluck the strings instead of bowing them.

flashcard_questions.q: At what interval does the backing vocalist harmonise in the last phrase of Verse 1 of Africa?

notes: 15 cards: 8 term-to-definition (conjunct, disjunct, trill, grace notes, syllabic, melisma, sequence, pizzicato), 2 marking-to-meaning (legato, staccato), 1 shape term, 1 notation card (tie), plus 3 example-to-feature cards drawn from the set work (chorus two-pitch range, B major pentatonic at bars 66–69, 3rd-below harmony in Verse 1). Set-work moments are named by bar and section, never by lyric. Dropped slur as a card because the tie card already fixes the distinction without interference.
